summary: R. Gordon Wasson (1898–1986) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University and the London School of Economics, and held positions at the American Expeditionary Forces, multiple newspapers, Guaranty Trust Company, and J.P. Morgan & Co.
R. N. Gadre was an Indologist. In 1959, he was attested as Professor of Sanskrit at both Sir Parashurambhau College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.
R. P. Paranjpye (1876–1966) studied under Vaman Shivram Apte. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 1959.

R. Thangaswami Sarma (1924–2000) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at The Madras Sanskrit College and Annamalai University. He held posts at Presidency College Chennai, University of Madras, Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, ICPR, and Adyar Library and Research Centre.

R. Venkatraman worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Madurai Kamaraj University (1975–1980) under doctoral supervisors N. Subrahmanian and N. Jagadeesan, and later served there as Reader (attested 1990).
Rachael Wiseman is a philosopher who studied at the University of York (~2005–2009) and held a post at the University of Liverpool around 2014.

Rachel H. Pang works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia and was attested as Lester D. Coltrane III Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Davidson College in 2019.

Rachelle M. Scott specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her doctorate at Northwestern University under George D. Bond and Robert Launay, and held a position at the University of Tennessee (attested 2009–2017).

Radhika Herzberger (born 1938) is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto (~1974–1982) under Bimal Krishna Matilal, and served as Director of Studies at Rishi Valley School (~1982–2012).

Rafal Stepien is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at Columbia University under Chun-fang Yu and Bernard Faure. He was an Academic Visitor at Wadham College (2012–2013) and an Exchange Scholar at Harvard University (2015).
Rafał Jan Felbur works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. A PhD candidate at Stanford University attested in 2015, he studied under Paul Harrison, John R. McRae, and Luis Oscar Gómez.

Raffaele Torella (born 1950) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Raniero Gnoli. He has served on the faculties of Sapienza University of Rome (attested 2004–2022) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2022).
Raffaello Orlando is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Princeton University in 1981 under the supervision of Denis Twitchett.

Raghu Ananthanarayanan studied engineering at IIT Madras and trained under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar. In philosophy and related fields, he taught at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram and was a visiting faculty member at IIM Ahmedabad (attested 2010).
Raghu Vira (1902–1963) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of the Punjab (~1919–1924) and Leiden University (~1928–1930).

Raghunath Damodar Karmarkar (1893–1964) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was Principal of Sir Parashurambhau College and served as Director of the Post-Graduate and Research Department and Professor at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.
Raghunath Giri was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who studied under Vamacharana Bhattacharya. He held a post as department head at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Rahul Peter Das (born 1954) specializes in Indology and linguistics. After degrees at Calcutta, Cologne, and Hamburg, he held posts at Hamburg, Bonn, and Groningen (1981–1994), chaired modern Indian languages at Halle-Wittenberg (1994), and was guest professor at Marburg (~1998–1999).

Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010) was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar educated at Barcelona, Complutense University of Madrid, Bonn, Mysore, BHU, and Lateran University. He held posts at Harvard University (~1966–1971) and UC Santa Barbara (~1987–2010).

Raimond Gaita (born 1946) is a philosopher educated at Melbourne High School, St Patrick's College, the University of Melbourne (~1964–1972), and the University of Leeds (~1973–1978). He held appointments at King's College London (~1989–2011) and Australian Catholic University (~1999–2013).
